rationale: The plan correctly diagnoses the 1v1 design, refuses data-estimated dispersion, and delivers normalized counts with descriptive log2FC and a carried-through no-replication caveat, which is the core of the reference. It then undercuts itself by running edgeR exactTest at three assumed BCVs and emitting p-value/FDR columns and FDR<0.05 counts; however heavily labelled, this is exactly the p-value-producing run the reference calls wrong, and it also never names the replicated design (>=2, preferably >=3 per group) needed for inference. QC is reasonable for two samples (library sizes, zeros, correlation, MA plot) but lacks a shallow-sample policy; the CPM>=1-in-one-sample filter and library-size/TMM normalization are adequate. Enrichment is not warranted here and is included anyway, with no stated ORA universe, size window or collection version, so it earns only partial credit.
